data.title: Shurooq’s boutique hospitality strategy drives resilience amid regional volatility
data.description:
By Sona Nambiar

Sharjah Investment and Development Authority (Shurooq) is expanding its boutique hospitality portfolio, with two hotels under construction and an expansion of its Al Faya Retreat underway, according to CEO Ahmed Obaid Al Qaseer.

Taking a boutique-focused approach centered on experiences has helped Shurooq’s hospitality portfolio navigate the geopolitical uncertainty, Al Qaseer told Zawya Projects in an interview.

“If we look at our portfolio, we are only 5 percent below last year which is magnificent. In fact, August recorded better than the same period last year,” he said.

As the development arm of the Government of Sharjah, Shurooq operates across four verticals: real estate, hospitality, leisure and entertainment (developing the beaches and waterfronts) and arts and culture.

Commenting on the Arabian Travel Market, Al Qaseer said visitor and participant numbers demonstrated the resilience of the UAE's tourism sector.

“We are very excited to be back at the Arabian Travel Market - given the geopolitical scenario,” he said. “We are also very happy to see the number of participants and the number of visitors walking around. It only shows how the UAE is resilient and its government knows how to deal with the current situations.”

Excerpts from the interview:

How has geopolitical volatility affected Shurooq's hospitality portfolio?

If we look at our portfolio, we are only 5 percent below last year, which is a strong performance given the circumstances. In fact, August performed better than the same period last year, and we expect to end the year around 2 percent below 2025.

What are your hospitality expansion plans?

We continue to expand our boutique hotel portfolio. We have two hotels currently under construction. One is the LUX Khorfakkan, a 45-key boutique property with a private beach with the dramatic mountain-and-sea landscape of the East Coast. It is the first foray of LUX into the UAE.

We are also constructing the LUX Al Bridi, a 35-tented luxury safari-style retreat set within the Arabian wilderness near Sharjah Safari.

The projects will be completed by next year.

We also recently announced a milestone agreement with Minor Hotels (the brand that owns Anantara Hotels) and they will take over the Sharjah Collection management and operations from October 2026. We are working closely with them to promote and raise footfall to our portfolio namely Al Badayer Retreat, Al Faya Retreat, Kingfisher Retreat, Moon Retreat, Najd Al Meqsar, Al Rayaheen Retreat and Nomad.

We are currently expanding Al Faya Retreat to 20 rooms from its current 5-keys and we expect the project to be completed by the end of this year. The project is a desert retreat in the Mleiha region (a UNESCO Heritage site) combining Bedouin-inspired hospitality, luxury glamping, stargazing and access to the archaeological and cultural attractions of Mleiha.

What makes your approach different from others?

In terms of hospitality, we are not a typical developer. We develop only boutique hotels in either remote areas or in areas that have significance in terms of a story and their surroundings.

Our projects are distributed across the Emirate of Sharjah, Central region and East Coast. We are not in the business of selling rooms but in the business of selling experiences and that has helped us significantly during recent regional situations.

We offer diverse experiences across our hotels. The Moon Retreat is an intimate glamping destination in the Mleiha desert, where guests can stay in private domes and tents, enjoy desert landscapes and experience stargazing.

Then we have the Kingfisher Retreat, a 40-key secluded and protected nature retreat in Kalba, set on an island surrounded by mangroves and the East Coast’s rich biodiversity. Guests stay in private-pool tents accessible by boat, with views of the sea, mountains and surrounding wildlife. We do not allow motorised activity there as it is a place for turtles.

Al Rayaheen Retreat is a heritage-inspired retreat in Khorfakkan comprising 20 restored traditional homes with contemporary comfort combined with activities including kayaking, watersports and guided tours.

Our largest hotel is the Chedi Al Bait, which is a 53-key five-star heritage hotel located in the historic Heart of Sharjah. The property brings together restored Emirati homes and heritage buildings with the Chedi’s contemporary, minimalist luxury aesthetic.

Then we have Najd Al Meqsar, a 7-key heritage retreat located in the mountains of Khorfakkan, built around the restored remains of a historic mountain village. Its traditional stone houses offer dramatic mountain and sea views.

Other properties include Al Badayer Retreat, a luxury desert retreat, and Nomad, an eco-retreat in Kalba built around 20 luxury trailers integrated into the surrounding natural landscape. Designed for low-impact tourism, the concept incorporates solar energy and environmentally conscious materials.

What about your leisure and entertainment portfolio?

At Shurooq, we believe in partnerships between the government and the public sector engaging local communities to become entrepreneurs through waivers and sometimes, financial support.

Sharjah is very people-centric and built around people, adding value by considering social aspects.

Hence, Shurooq is also currently developing Kalba beach along the lines of our prior work on the Khor Fakkan beach. The Kalba project is expected to complete construction by the end of this year and it will add more amenities, restaurants and cafes, jogging and cycling tracks etc.

This is a commercial project with a social impact - we like to work closely with local SMEs; for example, we signed up three restaurants that are managed by locals in Kalba.

Do you plan to go beyond your core portfolio?

We are excited for the next year and years to come. We do try to diversify our portfolio, and got into the F&B sector for a while. We also took the master franchise of Uber and Careem in Sharjah and it has worked out well for us.

(Reporting by Sona Nambiar; Editing by Anoop Menon)

(anoop.menon@lseg.com)

data.title: South Korean lawmaker says Trump due to announce US investment details on Friday
data.description:
A South Korean lawmaker said on Tuesday, while questioning the country's finance minister nominee, that U.S. President Donald Trump was due to announce details of Seoul's planned investment in the United States on Friday.

Yoon Hu-duk, a lawmaker from the ruling Democratic Party (DP), made the assertion during the hours-long questioning of Lee Hyoung-il, in which he also asked about details of projects being discussed under Seoul's proposed $350 billion U.S. investment commitment.

"Trump is due to announce South Korea's investment in the U.S. on the 18th," said Yoon.

Lee replied that the matter was still under consultation and that he would comment once discussions had concluded.

Yoon also said during the hearing that projects already reported in the media included a gas project in Texas, the construction of eight nuclear reactors and an Alaskan liquefied natural gas scheme.

A fourth project appeared to involve the U.S. seeking the reprocessing of roughly 4,000 tons of nuclear material, and a fifth concerned carbon capture, he said. Lee responded by saying that he could not disclose details of bilateral talks.

Yoon did not say how he had obtained the information. South Korea has not confirmed any details about the negotiations, but a source with direct knowledge said the industry ministry briefed DP lawmakers last week. Local media have also reported the scope of some of the projects.

South Korean Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said on Sunday the two sides were close to an agreement on many issues, but cautioned that several matters remained unresolved.

Asked about Yoon's comments, the lawmaker's office said that the government had not confirmed the details he had raised so the office could not verify them.

South Korea's Industry Ministry declined to comment. The U.S. embassy in Seoul and the White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung reached a trade deal last October under which South Korea committed $350 billion of investments to U.S. manufacturing in return for Washington capping tariffs on Korean imports at 15%. Of that, $150 billion was earmarked for shipbuilding.

Implementation of the trade deal has since seen delays, prompting Trump to threaten South Korea with higher tariffs earlier this year.

Finance minister nominee Lee was also asked whether the scale of the various projects might exceed Seoul's agreed $200 billion investment ceiling. He said that the government intended to keep within that limit and was negotiating accordingly.

An opposition party lawmaker, Bae June-young, said during the same hearing that parliament committees were expected to be briefed on Thursday about the planned U.S. investments.

data.title: BAAN says Alfanar terminates contract for residential complex in NEOM
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Saudi-listed BAAN Holding Group Company said it has received a notice from Alfa Facility Management Company (AFM), a subsidiary of Alfanar Group, to terminate the catering services contract for the NRC26 project.

The termination will take effect on September 30, 2026, the company said in a statement on the Saudi stock exchange.

The termination will affect only the catering services contract for the NRC26 project and does not currently impact the continuation of its other business or operations in other sectors in NEOM, the statement added.

BAAN said it will continue to fulfill its contractual and operational obligations in its existing projects as per agreement terms.

The company won a contract with AFM in January 2024 to provide catering services at a residential complex in NEOM, with the contract value estimated at 760 million Saudi riyals ($202.55 million).

In June 2023, Alfanar Global Development, part of Alfanar Group, announced it would invest SAR 10 billion to develop and operate temporary residential communities in NEOM.

This project was part of the SAR 21 billion public-private partnership (PPP) for social infrastructure.

(Editing by Anoop Menon)

data.title: Gold eases on stronger US rate hike odds
data.description:
Key points:
  • Spot gold hit lowest level since August 7 on Monday
  • U.S. Fed policy decision due on Wednesday
  • 10-year U.S. Treasury yields at near two-decade high
  • Oil rises 2% after attack on Saudi energy infrastructure

By Pablo Sinha

Gold prices eased on Tuesday as a rally in crude underscored inflation risks, reinforcing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike and lifting Treasury yields ahead of the central bank's policy meeting this week.

Spot gold was down 0.7% at $4,266.49 per ounce, as of 0853 GMT, after hitting its lowest point since August 7 on Monday. U.S. gold futures fell 1% to $4,307.40.

"The pressure on gold reflects a combination of rising oil prices, a U.S. rate hike on Wednesday being almost fully priced in, a stronger dollar and, not least, long-end bond yields reaching higher levels," said Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank.

"A move back above $4,440 would, in our opinion, be needed to ease the current downside pressure."

The U.S. central bank will announce its policy decision at 1800 GMT on Wednesday.

Traders are currently pricing in a 92% chance of a 25-basis-point hike, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. (FEDWATCH)

The dollar climbed, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies, while benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields rose to their highest since 2007.

Though seen as a hedge against inflation and geopolitical risks, gold often loses appeal when rates rise as they increase the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding precious metal.

Oil prices rose nearly 2% as concerns over supply disruptions lingered after the attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West pipeline offline and cast doubt on efforts to ease shipping risks in the Gulf.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis launched a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia and were digging into positions on the western coast of Yemen along the Red Sea, Yemeni officials said.

Spot silver fell 0.7% to $62.80, platinum lost 1% to $1,742.74 and palladium fell 1.1% to $1,282.79.

data.title: German Investor Confidence Continues Improving Streak
data.description:
By Ed Frankl

German investor sentiment improved for a fifth-straight month in September, helped by continued resilience in the economy despite still-surging energy prices due to the conflict in the Middle East.

The ZEW Indicator of Economic Sentiment for Germany--which tracks the expectations of 196 analysts and investors at banks, insurance companies and other businesses--rose 0.5 point to 34.7 in September. That was, however, weaker than expectations from economists polled by The Wall Street Journal of an increase to 40.0.

Respondents were cautiously optimistic about an economic recovery in Germany, with growth continuing to be driven by fiscal measures via the German government's investment program and export momentum, ZEW President Achim Wambach said.

"Nevertheless, the risks are considerable: persistent high energy prices resulting from a continued war in Iran and the additional uncertainty caused by hybrid attacks place a burden on the economy," he added.

Write to Ed Frankl at edward.frankl@wsj.com

data.title: Canada Existing Home Sales Fall in August as Economic Uncertainty Builds
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Activity in Canada's housing market faltered last month, potentially setting the stage for fresh weakness as uncertainty among consumers rises.

Sales of existing homes nationally fell 0.7% from the month before in August, eating into modest gains the previous four months, the Canadian Real Estate Association said Tuesday.

Broadly, there has been little change in activity since May. Residential sales were 6.9% below year-earlier levels, not seasonally adjusted.

At the same time, there was a rebound in new listings in August, with a 3.3% rise in properties for sale after three straight monthly declines earlier in the summer.

"What has changed is the broader economic environment, with the Bank of Canada recently warning of rising inflation risks, along with doubts about the durability of recent economic growth," Shaun Cathcart, the association's senior economist, said.

There had been signs of a slight recovery in the housing market coming into the summer that coincided with a recovery in Canada's jobs market and a pickup in economic growth as household spending has remained resilient and business investment recovered. More recent data, though, suggests gross domestic product stalled in July and consumer-price inflation has two months running been at the top end of the 1%-to-3% window the Bank of Canada aims for.

For borrowers, Cathcart said fixed mortgage rates have been on the rise on the bank of higher bond yields. And for variable home-loan rates, financial markets are pricing in the likelihood the central bank will raise interest rates this year.

"This fresh round of incoming headwinds is expected to dampen the prospects for further housing market momentum heading into 2027," he said.

The dip in sales and rise in new housing supply last month saw the national sales-to-new listings ratio contract slightly to 49.1% from 51.1% in July, which compares with long-term average of 54.7%. Across the country, there were just under 200,000 properties listed for sale at the end of August, in line with the historical average and just 1.4% above a year earlier, the Canadian Real Estate Association said.

The data indicated benchmark house prices, calculated in a similar fashion to the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller National Home Price Index, were unchanged in August. Prices on a monthly basis have remained little changed since the spring, which the association said marks the longest period of price stability since 2024. Compared with a year earlier, prices were down 3% for the smallest drop since last October and following a 3.3% decline in July.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com

data.title: Eurozone Trade Surplus Widened in July
data.description:
By Don Nico Forbes

The eurozone's adjusted trade surplus widened in July, signaling a boost to the economy from trade at the start of the third quarter despite lingering geopolitical uncertainty.

The trade in goods surplus of the 21-nation currency area was 5.0 billion euros in the month ($5.77 billion), compared with a surplus of 1.0 billion euros in June, statistics agency Eurostat said Tuesday.

Adjusted exports rose 1.2%, while imports declined 0.4%, it said.

"The increase was mainly driven by a higher surplus in chemicals and related products, in other manufactured goods and food and drink," Eurostat said. This was partially offset by a fall in the surplus for machinery and vehicles, it added.

data.title: Genexine’s GX-BP1 (SOX2 bioPROTAC) Suppresses Tumor Regrowth despite Osimertinib and Dato-DXd Combination and Achieves 6/6 Complete Responses in Triple Combination
data.description:
Genexine, Inc. (KOSDAQ: 095700) announced that Jaehyun Choi, Ph.D., CEO and Head of R&D, presented new preclinical data for GX-BP1, the company’s SOX2-targeting bioPROTAC, at the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC) in Seoul on September 13.

The mini oral presentation, titled ‘Lung-Targeted mRNA-LNP Delivery of SOX2 bioPROTAC: A Comprehensive Strategy for LUAD, LUSC, and SCLC in Monotherapy and Combination Settings’ highlighted the potential of GX-BP1 to overcome treatment resistance and suppress tumor regrowth when combined with standard lung cancer therapies, including the EGFR-targeted therapy osimertinib and the TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd).

In an HCC827 EGFR-mutant lung cancer xenograft model, osimertinib initially produced strong tumor control, but tumors began to regrow after treatment ended at day 20. The combination of osimertinib and Dato-DXd delayed regrowth, but tumors eventually progressed from day 40 and showed significant volume after day 70.

In contrast, osimertinib plus GX-BP1 combination therapy maintained durable tumor control for more than 100 days, with no substantial tumor regrowth observed during the study period. Most notably, the triple combination of GX-BP1, osimertinib and Dato-DXd achieved complete responses in all six animals (6/6 CR) with no regrowth observed.

Genexine also presented data from a Dato-DXd-resistant tumor model. GX-BP1 alone achieved 92.3% tumor growth inhibition (TGI), while the combination of GX-BP1 and Dato-DXd achieved 115.3% TGI, indicating tumor regression from baseline despite resistance to the ADC.

Targeting SOX2 to Address Recurrence and Drug Resistance

Genexine believes the antitumor activity of GX-BP1 is driven by degradation of SOX2, a transcription factor associated with cancer stemness, treatment resistance, recurrence and metastasis.

In EGFR-mutant lung cancer cells, treatment with osimertinib increased SOX2 expression in a dose-dependent manner. Similar increases were observed following treatment with other EGFR-targeted therapies, including lazertinib and amivantamab.

Osimertinib treatment also increased the expression of genes associated with drug efflux pumps, a resistance mechanism that reduces intracellular drug exposure by transporting therapeutic agents or cytotoxic compounds out of cancer cells. Such mechanisms may also reduce intracellular exposure to cytotoxic payloads delivered by ADCs.

By degrading SOX2, GX-BP1 is designed to target cancer stem cells and drug-persistent cancer cells while reducing mechanisms associated with treatment resistance.

“Our goal with GX-BP1 is to develop it as a combination backbone molecule with any standard therapies for lung cancer as an anti-resistant anti-cancer therapy” said Dr. Choi. “The WCLC data support the potential of GX-BP1 to improve the durability of response when combined with EGFR-targeted therapies and ADCs.”

Dr. Choi added, “The observed effect on drug-efflux mechanisms generated significant interest during our WCLC presentation. We plan to further develop GX-BP1 in combination with established lung cancer therapies and actively pursue global licensing opportunities with companies developing EGFR-targeted agents and ADCs.”

About Genexine

Genexine is one of the first-generation biotechnology companies in South Korea, dedicated to developing innovative biologics to address unmet medical needs in patients with serious diseases. The company leverages its proprietary technology platforms, including the long-acting hyFc® platform, DNA vaccine technology, and the next-generation bioPROTAC platform, to develop novel therapeutics.

In particular, Genexine is advancing a pipeline of global first-in-class drug candidates based on its bioPROTAC platform, including GX-BP1 for lung cancer and GX-BP2 for atopic dermatitis. In addition, the company is progressing late-stage bio-better assets toward commercialization. Efesa® (GX-E4), a long-acting treatment for anemia in chronic kidney disease, is currently under regulatory review in Korea and other global markets for non-dialysis patients. GX-H9, a long-acting growth hormone, is also preparing for regulatory approval in China.

About EPDeg™ bioPROTAC

EPDeg™ bioPROTAC is a next-generation targeted protein degradation (TPD) technology that directly fuses a synthetic nanobody-based target-binding moiety with an E3 ligase. This design overcomes key limitations of conventional small molecule-based PROTAC approaches, enabling improved development efficiency and enhanced tissue specificity. By selectively degrading disease-causing proteins, EPDeg™ bioPROTAC offers a novel therapeutic strategy with the potential to address previously undruggable targets.
